_README: Reference distributions used to shape the seeded demo dataset.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: these weights used to be magic numbers inline in
generate_narrative_data.py with a comment claiming they were
'population-weighted'. They were not derived from any source. Pulling them
out here makes the provenance of every number explicit and auditable, and
means replacing them with officially published figures is a DATA edit rather
HONESTY RULE: every entry carries a 'basis' and a 'source'. Do not change a
number without updating both. 'illustrative' means the value was chosen to
look plausible and is NOT sourced - it must never be described as official.
TO CALIBRATE AGAINST REAL DATA: replace the values, set basis to e.g.
'ncrb_crime_in_india_2022_table_3A', set source to the exact table and URL,
and set calibrated to true. The loader validates shape only, so any
consistent set of positive weights works.

_provenance.summary: District and crime-type mixes are ILLUSTRATIVE, not sourced from published crime statistics. They are shaped to be broadly plausible (property crime common, homicide rare; larger urban districts carry more volume) so the analytics demonstrate real behaviour, but no figure here should be presented as an official statistic.
known_gaps: District-level Karnataka crime counts are not available as a clean machine-readable download: ncrb.gov.in is behind bot validation, and 'Crime in India' publishes PDF tables. data.gov.in hosts NCRB datasets under the Govt Open Data License - India but district-level coverage skews to older years.
Crime-type shares are not mapped to NCRB IPC crime-head categories, so they are not directly comparable to published tables.
candidate_sources: NCRB 'Crime in India' annual report, state and city tables (PDF; 2022 volumes mirrored at archive.org/details/PARI.crime-in-india-2022-volume-ii)
data.gov.in NCRB catalogues, Govt Open Data License - India
Karnataka State Police / District Crime Record Bureau published figures

district_weights._note: Relative sampling weights, not counts. Only the ratios matter; the loader normalises them. Names must match the DISTRICTS list used by the seeder.
district_weights._source: none - chosen to be plausible, see _provenance.summary

crime_type_shares._note: Relative sampling weights across the seeded crime types.
crime_type_shares._source: none - chosen so property crime dominates and homicide is rare, which is directionally true of reported IPC crime but is NOT a sourced figure
